title: Motivation
coreMove: Turn a stalled obligation into a self-authored next move that the actor can choose and start.
sourcePressure: Robert Philippe can still understand his life after returning from South America, but his initiative collapses; the chapter connects that launch failure to locus of control, Marine boot camp, nursing-home rebellions, and a bias toward action.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating motivation as louder encouragement, stricter discipline, or a mood problem instead of a control-and-initiation problem.

sourceAnchors.name: Robert Philippe
sourceAnchors.detail: a high-output Louisiana businessman whose drive changes after a South America trip involving La Paz
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Robert Philippe still knew the shape of his life; what went missing was the small inner shove that turns knowing into doing.

sourceAnchors.name: Dr. Richard Strub
sourceAnchors.detail: finds normal vital signs, intact understanding, and normal IQ while Robert shows little drive
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Dr. Richard Strub could not solve Robert with the usual labels, because the facts were present and the launch was not.

sourceAnchors.name: MRI evidence of slight striatum damage
sourceAnchors.detail: the sidecar supports only a careful claim that MRI evidence points to slight damage in the striatum
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The striatum detail should land as a narrow clue about initiation, not as a grand theory of effort.

hook: Person at a meeting realizes the real lesson
The day starts with a dashboard
counterintuition: Productivity is not doing more faster
The problem is not effort but something deeper

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: a hospital discharge desk where patients keep missing one form before leaving
exampleSpecs.audience: a charge nurse trying to reduce repeated delays without barking orders
exampleSpecs.stakes: patients wait longer and nurses learn to wait for Sarah to fix every omission
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sarah moves the final-signature choice from her clipboard to the patient-facing tray and asks each nurse to choose the next discharge they will personally close before lunch
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A row of unsigned blue discharge folders leans against the printer

exampleSpecs.domain: a Montreal youth hockey practice where players freeze until the coach names every drill
exampleSpecs.audience: an assistant coach with twelve restless fifteen-year-olds
exampleSpecs.stakes: practice pace dies and players stop reading the ice for themselves
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Mathieu stops calling the next drill, lays three puck routes on the ice, and makes each line captain pick and run one route immediately
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Which route is yours?" Mathieu asks, holding the whistle at his side
mustAvoid: coach gives a speech about confidence

exampleSpecs.domain: a Toronto immigration clinic triaging appointment packets after a software outage
exampleSpecs.audience: a clinic coordinator whose volunteers wait for her every instruction
exampleSpecs.stakes: families lose appointment slots if packet checks stall
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Aanya contrasts the morning when volunteers waited with the afternoon when each volunteer chose one packet category and owned the first correction
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Aanya three hours to notice the quiet around the intake table

exampleSpecs.domain: a restaurant prep station before a Saturday dinner rush
exampleSpecs.audience: a sous-chef who has been over-directing new line cooks
exampleSpecs.stakes: prep slips into service because no cook starts without Thomas naming the next pan
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Thomas places the prep list beside six empty hotel pans and has each cook claim one pan and start the first cut before he says another word
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The smell of chopped parsley sits over six empty hotel pans

exampleSpecs.domain: a university lab where undergraduates wait for the postdoc to assign every reagent check
exampleSpecs.audience: a postdoc training first-year research assistants
exampleSpecs.stakes: an experiment loses the afternoon window when no one initiates setup
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Giulia asks assistants to predict which step will stall, then gives each one a chosen setup move they must begin
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What happens when everyone knows the protocol and no one owns the first pipette?
mustAvoid: letting the question hook replace the visible action beat

exampleSpecs.domain: a public library branch preparing for storm-day shelter service
exampleSpecs.audience: a branch manager with part-time staff waiting for instructions
exampleSpecs.stakes: residents will arrive cold before the shelter setup is ready
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Henrik turn a shelter checklist into five chosen posts so the staff can begin before the first family comes through the door
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You are looking at a shelter checklist while sleet taps the library windows

skillTargets: recognize a launch problem even when the person already has information
choose interventions that restore real agency instead of adding pressure
distinguish cosmetic choice from control that changes the next move

tryThisNowSpec: Pick one task you keep treating as something you should do and rewrite only the next 60 seconds as a choice you will make: open the file, make the call, or move the first object.
